{{Short description|Soviet American mathematician}}
{{For|the Russian field hockey player|Aleksandr Goncharov}}
[[File:Alexander Goncharov.jpg|thumb|220px|Alexander Goncharov]]
'''Alexander B. Goncharov''' (born April 7, 1960) is a Soviet American [[mathematician]] and the Philip Schuyler Beebe Professor of Mathematics at [[Yale University]]. He won the [[EMS Prize]] in 1992.

Goncharov won a gold medal at the [[International Mathematical Olympiad]] in 1976. He attained his [[doctorate]] at [[Lomonosov Moscow State University]] in 1987, under supervision of [[Israel Gelfand]] with thesis ''Generalized conformal structures on manifolds''.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://research.brown.edu/pdf/1106970220.pdf?nocache=498919904 |title=Curriculum Vitae |access-date=2011-11-08 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120425152413/http://research.brown.edu/pdf/1106970220.pdf?nocache=498919904 |archive-date=2012-04-25 |url-status=dead }}</ref> Goncharov was an Invited Speaker at the 1994 [[International Congress of Mathematicians]] and gave a talk ''[[Polylogarithm|Polylogarithms]] in arithmetic and geometry''.

In 2019, Goncharov was appointed the Philip Schuyler Beebe Professor of Mathematics at Yale University,<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://news.yale.edu/2019/05/28/alexander-goncharov-named-beebe-professor-mathematics|title=Alexander Goncharov named the Beebe Professor of Mathematics|date=2019-05-28|website=YaleNews|language=en|access-date=2019-06-28}}</ref> as well as the Gretchen and Barry Mazur Chair at the [[Institut des hautes études scientifiques]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.ihes.fr/en/special-day-journee-gretchen-barry-mazur/|title=Special Day 'Journée Gretchen & Barry Mazur'|date=2019-06-25|website=IHES|language=en-US|access-date=2019-06-28}}</ref>

[[Vesselin Dimitrov]] was a PhD student of his.<ref>{{MathGenealogy|44006}}</ref>
